波特姆金注意到——并欣赏——他外在的变化。他显然很满意地报告说，许久未见的亲戚和儿时玩伴会惊呼他变得判若两人。波特姆金大学学习期间的照片也显示他有所变化：他穿着西装打着领带，自信地面对镜头。然而，尽管有所有这些外部变化的迹象，他仍强调他转变的真正所在地和动力是内在的，在他的思想和灵魂之中。他坚持认为他的进步是合乎规律的——它符合马克思主义的辩证唯物主义和历史唯物主义规律。

Potemkin noticed—and appreciated—that he was changing outwardly. With evident satisfaction he reported that relatives and childhood friends whom he had not seen in a long time would exlaim that he had changed beyond recognition. Photographs of Potemkin during the years of his university studies show him changed as well: he appears dressed in a suit with tie and confidently faces the camera. Yet for all these external signs of change he stressed that the real locus and dynamic of his transformation were inward, in his mind and soul. And he insisted that his progression was lawful—that it corresponded to the Marxist laws of dialectical and historical materialism.

这一点在1935年秋季记录的一篇日记中变得显而易见，这篇日记以这样的话开头：“我内心生活的主要来源是我童年时期的贫困和匮乏经历。”波特姆金接着描述了他被母亲和姐姐派去“以基督之名”乞讨的经历：“才七岁，我就饱受残酷的嘲笑和讥讽……冬天我没去上学，我什么衣服也没有……童年时期通常的无忧无虑的游戏与我擦肩而过。”此时，波特姆金的回溯性视角拓宽了，他的主观自我故事被一个宏观历史叙述所补充：“代代相传的对精神和道德自由的物质暴力，在注定物质贫困的人们心中灌输了精神奴役、智力低下和意志薄弱。世代相传地丧失了对自身人类美德的认知、对自身美德及其自由发展的信念。正是这些困扰我的意识，激起了我的愤怒和反抗的意志。”
这些以及其他自传段落与马克思主义的无产阶级历史产生共鸣，无产阶级被资本主义制度奴役，然后奋起反抗压迫者。当波特姆金写到他自己的新生意识和反叛意志时，他将自己写入了无产阶级普遍叙事以及痛苦与反抗、匮乏与丰裕、一无所有与成为一切的辩证法之中，这些共同构成了其神话般的历史。

This becomes apparent in a diary entry recorded in the fall of 1935, which began with the words: “The primary source of my internal life was my experience of poverty and deprivations in childhood.” Potemkin then described being sent by his mother and sister to beg “‘in the name of Christ’”: “Just seven years old, I’m showered with cruel ridicule and mocking insults . . . I don’t go to school in the winter, I have nothing to wear . . . The usual carefree games of childhood passed me by.” At this point Potemkin’s retrospective frame widened, as the story of his subjective self was supplemented by a macrohistorical account: “The material violence committed against mental and moral freedom from generation to generation inculcated spiritual enslavement, feeblemindedness, and weakness of will in people doomed to material poverty. An inherited loss of a sense of one’s own human virtues and of faith in one’s own virtues and their free development. That is what troubled my consciousness and stirred my will to indignation and protest.”

These and other autobiographical passages resonate with the Marxist history of the proletariat, subjugated by the capitalist system but then rising up against its oppressors. When Potemkin wrote about his own emerging consciousness and rebellious will, he inscribed himself into a universal narrative of the proletariat and the dialectic of suffering and rebellion, deprivation and fullness, being nothing and becoming everything that undergirded its mythical history.

马克思主义无产阶级元叙事对波特姆金自我形象的重要性，可以从他的姑妈或姨妈看到侄子廖尼亚（小名）变成了一个穿着西装打领带的未来工程师时表现出的惊讶，而他对此做出的愤怒反应中衡量出来。显然，在他年轻时，她“没有看透贫困的外壳”来认识到他的潜力。“不！”他向日记中惊呼道。“我进入学院绝非偶然，这是社会主义革命的必然结果，它将我们从底层提升，并将我们抬高到他们之上……我们的意志是胜利的……只有我们这些贫困和难以置信苦难的子女才能而且必须创造新社会……只有我们被赋予了……给人类一个真正绽放的机会的使命。”

波特姆金深刻地将马克思列宁主义辩证法视为个人生活方式。辩证唯物主义 (diamat)——马克思主义关于自然、社会和意识在持续斗争中合乎规律发展的科学——对他来说，不仅仅是从教科书中学到的规定性世界观；它是共产主义基本教义的核心，因此具有切实可行的生命创造效应，将他过去和现在的经历、思想和行动统一成一个有凝聚力、有目的的传记。辩证法是他生命的红线，它将看似不连贯、偶然的冲动和行动联系起来并加以引导，统一他自我的各种表现。他自我的真相蕴含在其辩证发展之中，并在回顾性的审视中，在他审视自己的发展并重读日记中过去的段落时被揭示出来。在确立自我的真相时，波特姆金特别区分了心理学和历史。尽管有时他认为自己是受“心理动机”驱动的，但深入的反思帮助他认识到，他生命中的驱动力是他的自觉意志，它是历史性的，并受马克思主义辩证法规律的指导。这解释了他不断展开的生活的“连续性和目的性”的本质。

The importance of the Marxist metanarrative of the proletariat for Potemkin’s self-image can be gauged from his angry reaction when his aunt expressed surprise at seeing her nephew Lyonya transformed into an aspiring engineer dressed in suit and tie. Clearly in his youth she “had not seen through the shell of poverty” to recognize his potential. “No!” he exclaimed to his diary. “It is not by sheer chance that I am in the institute, it is the necessary consequence of the socialist revolution, which raised us up from below and elevated us above their heads . . . Our will is triumphant . . . Only we children of poverty and incredible hardship must and can create the new society . . . Only we are granted the mission of . . . giving mankind a chance to really bloom.”

Potemkin was deeply invested in Marxist-Leninist dialectics as a personal way of life. Dialectial materialism (diamat)—the Marxist science of the lawful development of nature, society, and consciousness in an ongoing process of struggle—to him signified more than a pre-scribed worldview learned from textbooks; it was the core of the Communist catechism and as such had tangible life-creating effects, unifying his past and present experiences, thoughts, and actions into a cohesive and purposeful biography. Dialectics was the red thread of his life, tying together and directing seemingly disjointed, accidental impulses and actions and unifying the various appearances of his self. The truth about his self was contained in its dialectical progression, and it was disclosed in the retrospective gaze, in the act of taking stock of his development and rereading past passages from his diary. In establishing the truth about himself, Potemkin made a point of distinguishing between psychology and history. Although at times he believed that he was propelled by “psychological motives,” intense reflection helped him realize that the driving force in his life was his conscious will, which was historical and directed by the laws of Marxist dialectics. This explained the “sequential and purposeful” nature of his unfolding life.
除了是波特姆金自我观念不可或缺的一部分外，掌握辩证法也是他在斯大林主义社会中获得认可和成功的关键。他在日记中报告说，辩证唯物主义老师对班级的表现不满意。作为学生干部，波特姆金决定为需要思想训练的同龄人组织集体学习课程。为此，他甚至制作了一本186页的辩证唯物主义手写教科书。

在随后的辩证唯物主义和历史唯物主义口试中，波特姆金被要求在全班同学面前与最优秀的辩证唯物主义学生竞争。最优秀的学生首先发言并获得了好成绩。然后轮到波特姆金。在全班同学的喧闹支持下（这是一个重要细节，因为波特姆金对自我人格的集体主义基础十分敏感），他展现出对“黑格尔哲学的本质”的惊人理解，以至于老师不得不重新考虑他早先的断言，即他不会给任何普通人，甚至“上帝本人”，打最高分，而只会给那个“能从天上摘下星星”的人——这指的是普罗米修斯，马克思主义无产阶级的神话先驱。在教员委员会面前，这位老师宣称波特姆金是“精通马克思主义的领军人物”。

Besides being integral to Potemkin’s conception of self, mastery of dialectics was also a key to his recognition and success in Stalinist society. In the diary he reported that the teacher of diamat was dissatisfied with the performance of the class. As student leader, Potemkin resolved to organize collective learning sessions for his peers in need of ideological training. For this purpose he even produced a handwritten textbook on diamat, numbering 186 pages.

At a subsequent oral exam in dialectical and historical materialism, Potemkin was called upon to compete against the best student of diamat in front of the class. The best student started first and received a good grade. Then it was Potemkin’s turn. With clamorous support from the whole class (an important detail, given Potemkin’s sensitivity to the collectivist underpinnings of selfhood), he displayed such an impressive knowledge of “the essence of Hegelian philosophy” that the instructor had to reconsider his earlier assertion that he would not give the highest grade to any ordinary human, or even to “God himself,” but only to the one “who would grab stars from the sky”—a reference to Prometheus, the mythical forefather of the Marxist proletariat. In front of a faculty commission the instructor declared that Potemkin was a “leader in mastery of Marxism.”

波特姆金在日记中写道，在一次即兴演讲后，他“备受关注”：女孩们抓住他的手臂，他，这个“从未被爱过，事实上也无可被爱之人”。他接着说：“我内心那种不被任何一个女孩接受的爱，以对社会的热爱以及对社会伟大热爱的光明喜悦的形式迸发出来。我不仅要让那个吸引我的女孩爱上我，而且整个社会也会爱我、尊重我。”即使这种关于辩证唯物主义及其影响的评论，也充满了辩证法的启示。过去那个丑陋、微不足道、无法找到个人爱情的人，现在踏上了个人自我训练的道路，拥抱了社会，反过来，也获得了社会给予的爱，这种爱远远优于他曾对某些女孩的爱——超越任何个人爱情观念。这种思维模式表明，他现在感到自己在个人发展中实现了幸福的综合，事实上，在他一篇自传性日记条目旁边的空白处，他用小字写道：“发展之胜利。”

After one of his improvised lectures, Potemkin noted in his diary, he was “showered with attention”: the girls seized him by the arms, him, whom “no one ever loved and in fact who had nothing to be loved for.” He went on: “The love in me which was not accepted by a single girl flared up in the form of a love for society and the bright joy of a great love of society. Not only will I compel a girl who fascinates me to love me, but all society will love and respect me too.” Even this commentary on diamat and its effects was dialectically informed. He who in the past had been ugly, insignificant, incapable of finding personal love, had embarked on a path of individual self-training, had embraced society, and now in turn was rewarded with a love from society that was infinitely superior to the love he had once felt for certain girls—superior to any notion of individual love. This pattern of thinking suggested that he now felt he had achieved a happy synthesis in his personal development, and indeed, in the margin next to one of the autobiographical diary entries he wrote in small letters: “triumph of development.”

zh: 在污秽中保持纯洁

children: 1934年秋天，当列昂尼德·波特姆金与《矿工风暴》编辑见面并决定将自己塑造成一个模范社会主义人格时，他纲领性地指出：“我将把自己看作一个崭露头角的作家。我知道该怎么做。计划已经制定好。剩下的唯一事情就是执行它，……完全实现这个项目。”将近两年后，即1936年9月，他决定终止这个项目。当他乘坐图尔格涅夫号蒸汽船在伏尔加河上航行，接近高尔基市时，他思考着他的“文学梦想”。他意识到，与当年早些时候去世的伟大马克西姆·高尔基相比，他的目标过于雄心勃勃，他未能利用日记来展现他丰富的内心世界。相反，他决定通过“书面和口头”交流与他人分享他的“心灵世界及其成就”。

回顾过去五年的日记，波特姆金试图理解它为何出现以及是关于什么的。他解释说，当他还是青少年时，没有人关注他或尊重他。这促使他写日记并将自己封闭在“自我分析的领域”中。对于孤独或身心有缺陷、缺少现实中的同志帮助他们自我分析和自我改造的人来说，日记是一种替代伴侣。现在他作为一名领袖被广泛关注，他可以“自信而深情地将我内心世界的宝藏呈现给人们”。波特姆金尤其想到了女性朋友。对他而言，女性是“精神和创造性生活中的同志”。与女性朋友的亲密对话最能表达灵魂的生活，并能激发他作为一名共产党员职业所需的更高层次的审美情趣。但要找到一个分享他柏拉图式愿景的女性并不容易——他所有的女性朋友想的都是如何让他娶她们。
波特姆金的这本日记到此为止。然而，有一份资料可以揭示他接下来两年，即1937年和1938年的个人生活。那是他与伊拉·日尔科娃的往来书信，共157页，伊拉是一位在高尔基市学习文学的年轻女性。她似乎是距离他理想中的女性灵魂伴侣最近的人，几乎已经达到他所能期望的程度。
在他写给日尔科娃的信中，波特姆金始终致力于人格塑造的议程和新人的理想。通过在朋友之间互动交流中展现这些问题，这些信件阐明了友谊的意义以及两位年轻的苏联公民所理解的隐私的轮廓和重要性。

In the fall of 1934, when Leonid Potemkin met with the editor of the Miner’s Storm and decided to represent himself as a model socialist personality, he stated programmatically: “I will recognize myself as an emerging writer. I know what to do. The plan is worked out. The only thing left to do is to execute it, . . . to completely realize the project.” Almost exactly two years later, in September 1936, he decided to break off the project. While cruising the Volga on the steamship Turgenev and nearing the city of Gorky, he contemplated his “literary dreams.” He realized that in comparison with the great Maxim Gorky, who had died earlier that year, his goals had been overly ambitious and he had failed at using the diary for the representation of his rich inner world. Instead he resolved to share his “psychic world and its achievements” in “written and oral” communications with other people.

Looking back at his diary of the past five years, Potemkin tried to understand why it had come into being and what it had been about. When he was an adolescent, he explained, no one had paid attention to him or shown him respect. This had incited him to keep a diary and lock himself up in a “sphere of self-analysis.” Diaries were surrogate companions for lonely or deformed people who lacked real-life comrades to help them carry out their work of self-analysis and self-transformation. Now that he was widely noticed as a leader, he could “confidently and with affection turn over to people the treasure of my inner world.” Potemkin had in mind female friends in particular. A woman to him was a “comrade in spiritual and creative life.” Intimate dialogue with a female friend best expressed the life of the soul and would stir him into the heightened aesthetic sensibility essential for his vocation as a Communist. But it was not easy to find a woman who shared his platonic vision—all his female friends thought about was how to get him to marry them.

It is with these thoughts that Potemkin’s diary notebook ends. There is, however, a source that sheds light on his personal life for the next two years, 1937 and 1938. It is his correspondence, 157 pages of it, with Ira Zhirkova, a young woman who was studying literature in Gorky. She seems to have come as close to his ideal of a female soul mate as he could possibly expect.

In his letters to Zhirkova, Potemkin remained committed to the agenda of personality formation and the ideal of the new man. In showing these issues in the interactive exchange between friends, the letters shed light on the meaning of friendship and the contours and significance of privacy as understood by two young Soviet citizens.

波特姆金是通过他姐姐认识日尔科娃的，他姐姐于1932年离开斯维尔德洛夫斯克，到高尔基建筑工程学院学习。两人相识后，波特姆金主动与她通信。尽管信件中流露出的爱意和思念可能暗示两人是恋人，但波特姆金后来坚称这种关系完全是柏拉图式的。通信的主要主题和目的是精神交流。两位通信者都试图展现他们内心深处最温柔的情感以及对道德纯洁的追求。正如日尔科娃所说，这些信件旨在帮助他们进行灵魂教育。他们都强调自己在表达感情时的真诚。针对伊拉在一封信中指责他将真实情感隐藏在“官方辞令”之后，列昂尼德宣称他除了他意识和灵魂中的东西，从未写过其他任何东西：“一封信是我内心世界情感最真诚的表达。”
为了强调他们的真诚以及彼此的信任，波特姆金和日尔科娃也互相交换日记阅读。

Potemkin met Zhirkova through his sister, who had left Sverdlovsk in 1932 to study at the Gorky Institute for Construction Engineering, and he initiated their correspondence after this encounter. While expressions of affection and longing in the letters could suggest that the two were lovers, Potemkin later insisted that the relationship was entirely platonic. The principal theme and purpose of the correspondence was spiritual communion. Both correspondents sought to exhibit their innermost, most tender emotions and their striving for moral purity. As Zhirkova put it, the letters were to aid in the education of their souls. Both emphasized how sincere they were in the display of their feelings. In response to Ira’s accusation that in one letter he was hiding his true sentiments behind “official rhetoric,” Leonid declared that he had never written anything other than what was in his consciousness and soul: “A letter is the most sincere expression of the emotions of my inner world.”
To underscore their sincerity as well as their trust in each other, Potemkin and Zhirkova also gave each other their diaries to read.
除了公开展示个人丰富的内心世界，波特姆金和日尔科娃在这些信件中进行的“灵魂解剖”旨在监控和完善他们的精神进步。在十月革命二十周年之际，列昂尼德赞扬了“社会主义文化温室的辉煌而宏伟的绽放”，同时他祝愿在革命当年出生的伊拉“你的精神能力得到充分而宏伟的绽放，为这个温室增添更大的美”。

有时他们的交流揭示了意识形态上的分歧，这尤其促使波特姆金批评他犯错的伴侣的偏差。他严厉而分析性地阅读她的信件，仿佛在批改学生关于历史唯物主义的论文：“我终于完成了对你信件的详细审查。现在让我来得出一般性结论。”在一封信中，他列举了她提出的一些意识形态上可疑的言论，例如：“大自然绝不是为人类幸福而创造的，人类也完全无法创造幸福。当代人情不自禁地想要逃离这个不幸的时代。”列举这些不利于她的言论后，他呼吁她遵从意识形态的理性：
伊拉，我现在非常疲惫，深夜时分来解释这些。你看，你不能从任何一种观点出发写作。我不想对这些显而易见的谬误进行批评，因为我希望你自己能驳斥它们。我不会随便得出结论，而是从我所属社会的角度得出的结论，我对你以不同的眼光看待我的指责感到不满，正如你所说。如果它们不能迫使你重新考虑，那就更甚了。我心痛地写下这些。

就伊拉而言，她温和地责备她的朋友是一个“无可救药的梦想家”：“你把一切都理想化了。我完全同意你关于生活的论点……但对你的话必须加上‘那应该是这样的’，而对我的话则是‘事实就是如此，仅此而已’。”作为回应，波特姆金告诉她，她归因于他的理想主义是一种历史上过时的立场，进步人士执着于此，以此作为“暂时逃避可怕现实”的方式；相比之下，他所倡导的理想正在社会主义建设中实现，他的热情建立在这样的认知之上：他自己将是第一批“在现实生活中看到理想首次化身”的人之一。

但波特姆金也承认了他的世界观中的弱点，并向日尔科娃寻求建议：“伊拉，我亲爱的，请听我这颗无用的心的忏悔。”他承认他“最新一轮的抑郁”之类的发作。在获得了一切——最高分数、作为学生领袖的认可，以及“对一个女人的盲目迷恋”——之后，他再也没有什么目标可以追求了，他“灵魂”的“火焰”熄灭了：“啊，矿业学院，你的一切范围之内再也无法点燃我的灵魂了。我像一只吃完奶油的猫，带着不悦的表情看着盘子里剩下的东西。不，我不是工程师，也不是地质学家——我的内心阻碍着我。”

Beyond the open display of the individual’s rich inner world, the “anatomy of the soul” that Potemkin and Zhirkova performed in these letters was done for the purpose of monitoring and perfecting their spiritual progression. On the twentieth anniversary of the October Revolution, Leonid lauded the “splendid and majestic blossoming of the greenhouse of socialist culture,” and in the same breath he wished Ira, who had been born the year of the revolution, “full and majestic blossoming of your spiritual capacity, to add even greater beauty to this greenhouse.”

At times their exchange revealed ideological disagreements, which impelled Potemkin in particular to criticize the deviations of his erring partner. He read her letters sternly and analytically, as if grading a student’s papers on historical materialism: “At last I have completed a detailed review of your letter. Now let me draw general conclusions.” In one letter he listed ideologically questionable statements she had made, such as: “Nature in no way is created for human happiness and the human being is utterly incapable of forging happiness. Contemporary people cannot help wanting to run away from this unfortunate time.” Following this incriminating evidence came his call to ideological reason:

Ira, I am explaining this in a very tired state, late at night. You see, you cannot write from just any point of view. I do not want to give you my criticism of these glaring untruths because I hope that you yourself will refute them. I do not draw just any conclusions, but conclusions from the perspective of the society to which I belong, and I am displeased that you look at my reproofs, as you put it, with different eyes. And even more so if they do not force you to reconsider. I write this with pain in my heart.

For her part, Zhirkova gently chided her friend as an “incorrigible dreamer”: “You idealize everything. I completely agree with your arguments about life . . . But to your words one must add ‘that’s the way it ought to be,’ and to mine ‘that’s the way it is, that’s that.’” In response, Potemkin informed her that the idealism she attributed to him was a historically outdated position that progressive-minded people clung to as a way to “escape dreadful reality for a moment”; by contrast, the ideals he invoked were being realized in the construction of socialism, and his enthusiasm was founded on the knowledge that he himself would be among the first to “see the first incarnation of the ideal in real life.”

But Potemkin also confessed to weaknesses in his worldview and asked Zhirkova for advice: “Ira, my darling, please hear the confession of my worthless heart.” He admitted to a “latest [bout of] depression” of sorts. Having attained everything—highest grades, recognition as a student leader, and “blind attraction to a woman”—he had no more goals to strive for, and the “blaze” of his “soul” was extinguished: “O, Mining Institute, nothing within your scope is capable of inflaming my soul anymore. I’m like a cat that ate the cream and gazes at what’s left on the plate with an unhappy expression. No, I’m not an engineer, nor a geologist—my heart stands in the way.”

波特姆金的痛苦可能被诊断为一种乌托邦式忧郁症。如果他的自我意识是历史地定义的，如果他因此在成为的过程中实现了自我，那么理想的实现就无法提供持久的满足感。相反，它损害了他的自我意识，削弱了他的意志力，而他的意志力正是在追求更高目标的奋斗中产生的。乌托邦式忧郁症在20世纪20年代不可能困扰苏联公民，那时共产主义社会的乌托邦理想与不纯洁的当前秩序之间如此明显遥远。然而，一旦社会主义被宣布已经实现，这种形式的忧郁症就变得可能了。它的爆发表明，这位共产党员的意志力有所下降，屈服于他失控身体的诱惑。如果他不能下定决心与他残余的旧自我作斗争，那么他朋友的责任就是帮助他。作为波特姆金的倾诉对象，日尔科娃责备他“悲观主义”和“缺乏勇气及对自己力量的信心”。任何抑郁都会反射性地引发自我谴责，从而伴随着对重新行动的呼唤。

对波特姆金而言，这些相互的坦白和纠正构成了他与日尔科娃关系的核心：“我从我们的友谊中获得如此多的满足，因为它使我们能够理解、分享内心世界的生活，并互相帮助评估我们的长处，以便明智地利用它们。友谊应该帮助一个人纠正缺点，发展人格文化，过上有意识、有抱负的生活。”波特姆金与日尔科娃通信的中心目的是建立一种共产主义式的友谊。朋友之间的精神契合应被用于相互人格塑造以及追求一种理性主义的、忠于意识形态的生活。通过分享“灵魂的共同语言”，朋友们可以互相帮助发现并克服个人缺陷。

Potemkin’s affliction might be diagnosed as a case of utopian melancholia. If his sense of self was defined historically, and if he thus realized himself in the act of becoming, attainment of the ideal could not provide lasting fulfillment. On the contrary, it undermined his sense of self and undercut his willpower, which was generated in the very striving toward higher goals. Utopian melancholia could not have afflicted Soviet citizens in the 1920s, when the utopian ideal of Communist society was so clearly distant from the impure present order. Once socialism was declared to have come into being, however, this form of melancholia became possible. Its outbreak was a sign that the Communist in question had slipped in willpower and surrendered to the temptations of his uncontrolled body. If he could not bring himself to fight his re-sidual old self, it was the duty of his friend to help. Acting as Potemkin’s confessor, Zhirkova chastised him for “pessimism” and a “lack of courage and confidence in your strength.” Any depression reflexively unleashed self-accusation and thus was enjoined by a call for renewed action.

For Potemkin these mutual confessions and corrections formed the essence of his relationship with Zhirkova: “I derive so much gratification from our friendship because it allows us to understand, share the life of the inner world, and help each other evaluate our strengths in order to use them intelligently. Friendship ought to help one correct flaws, develop the culture of personality, and live a conscious, aspiring life.” The central purpose of Potemkin’s correspondence with Zhirkova was to forge a Communist type of friendship. The spiritual affinity between friends was to be used for mutual personality formation and the pursuit of a rationalist, ideologically committed life. Sharing a “common language of the soul,” friends could help each other detect and overcome personal deficiencies.

波特姆金与日尔科娃之间的友谊具有教益和示范性，因此必须展现在众人面前。尽管两位通信者都强调了彼此之间完全的真诚，但他们从未将他们的作品视为一种私密的存在，即一个与公共价值观截然不同的隐藏、秘密领域。一张波特姆金坐在矿业学院阅览室的照片在这方面具有启发性。正如他后来解释的，在写完他写给日尔科娃的第一批信件之一后，他把它读给他的朋友尼古拉·阿列伊尼科夫听（图中也显示了他）。尼古拉在信中“注意到了一些有趣的东西”，并敦促列昂尼德抄写一份保存下来。正如照片所示，波特姆金与日尔科娃的通信在他在学院与朋友分享的半私人舞台上蓬勃发展。这封信的写作不仅受到同学（尼古拉和摄影师）的监督，也受到年轻列宁的监督，列宁的雕像装饰着阅览室。背景中的墙报强调了私密信件与共产主义意识形态之间的联系，暗示列昂尼德写给伊拉的信件是对报纸上社会主义生活颂歌的阐述。
波特姆金和日尔科娃的真诚姿态必须置于他们开始通信时普遍存在的怀疑、告发和强迫忏悔的背景之下。通过这个视角来看，他们所实践的感伤主义模式可以被解读为一种道德净化和赦免的形式，对其身心自保至关重要。日尔科娃经常提到她深夜写信，他们都暗示他们因教育、工作以及社会和文化活动的时间表而感到疲惫不堪。正如伊拉在一封信中写道：
我现在工作堆积如山，自己简直连一分钟空闲时间都没有。上午在学院，白天跑腿办事；下午4点开始工作，然后7点半去上外语课程。我去看戏，看电影，阅读文学，当然也提升自己。有时这样的生活有点累人，但总的来说我很满意……我（这封信）是在文学课上写着。
这些经过深思熟虑、精心构思的信件中崇高的灵魂语言，是在一种急躁的学习、狂热的建设以及针对两面派和人民隐藏敌人的不间断政治运动的环境中产生的。

The edifying and exemplary qualities of Potemkin’s friendship with  Zhirkova demanded to be put on display. While both correspondents stressed their total sincerity toward each other, they never conceived of their writings as private in the sense of a hidden, secret realm distinct from public values. A photograph of Potemkin sitting in the reading room of the Mining Institute is suggestive in this regard. As he later explained, after writing one of his first letters to Zhirkova, he read it to his friend Nikolai Aleinikov (also shown in the picture). Nikolai “noticed something interesting” in the letter and urged Leonid to make a copy to keep. As the photo illustrates, the correspondence with Zhirkova thrived on the semi-private stage Potemkin shared with his friends at the institute. The writing of the letter was monitored not only by fellow students (Nikolai and the photographer) but also by the young Lenin, whose statue adorned the reading room. The wall newspapers in the background underscore the link between the intimate letter and Communist ideology, suggesting that Leonid’s letters to Ira elaborated on the newspaper’s odes to socialist life.

Potemkin’s and Zhirkova’s gestures of sincerity must be situated in the context of the suspicion, denunciations, and forced confessions that pervaded the time when they took up their correspondence. Seen through this lens, the sentimentalist mode they practiced can be read as a form of moral cleansing and absolution indispensable for their physical and spiritual self-preservation. Zhirkova frequently mentioned that she wrote the letters late at night, and they both alluded to being exhausted by their schedules of education, work, and social and cultural activities. As Ira noted in one letter:

I’m up to my neck in work right now and have literally not a free minute for myself. The morning in the institute, errands during the day; at work starting at 4 p.m. and from there to foreign language courses at 7:30 p.m. I go to the theater, the movies, read literature, and of course work on myself. Sometimes such a life is a bit exhausting, but all in all I’m satisfied . . . I’m writing [this] during the literature class.

The exalted language of the soul in these thoughtful, crafted letters was produced in an environment of impatient learning, frenzied construction, and incessant political campaigning against double-dealers and hidden enemies of the people.

政治恐怖的背景以间接的方式出现在波特姆金的日记和通信中。他对健康、强大、充满活力的生活的拥抱，带有一种隐藏的阴影，即大多是含蓄的，但有时也直接而严厉地谴责那些弱小、过时的社会现象。在1935年初，他提到大学里一个关于“季诺维也夫集团的下流败类”的公开演讲。伊拉罕见地直接提到了政治压迫：“利奥，我很高兴你是那些我尊重的人之一，我在你面前鞠躬，睁大眼睛仰望你——因为你是在极致的污秽中，保持了自身纯洁的少数人之一。”因此，两位通信者都赞扬了他们对精神美和纯洁的理想，以及他们对光明未来的憧憬，对抗着一个大部分未被提及但却隐约可见的、由当下不纯洁、斗争和死亡构成的背景。
在政治恐怖的背景下，波特姆金和日尔科娃的友谊具有某些浪漫主义内涵。与将友谊培养成逃避资产阶级世界利己主义的避难所的德国浪漫主义类似，这些年轻的苏联公民参与他们对美德和纯洁的相互投射，部分是为了保护自己免受政治领域污染性的侵蚀。然而，波特姆金并没有将友谊培养成与社会领域截然对立的东西；相反，他始终坚持个人感情必须服从他建设新秩序的首要承诺。

A background of political terror appears in oblique ways in Potemkin’s diary and correspondence. His embrace of a healthy, strong, vitalist life carried a hidden shadow, a mostly implicit but at times direct and harsh condemnation of weak, outdated social phenomena. In early 1935 he mentioned a public presentation at the university devoted to the “low-life scum of the Zinoviev group.” A rare direct reference to political repression came from Ira: “Leo, I’m so happy that you are one of those people I respect, before whom I bow down and on whom I look with wide eyes—because you are one of the few who, amid utter dirt, has preserved a purity within yourself.” Both correspondents thus extolled their ideals of spiritual beauty and purity, and their vision of a bright future, against a largely unmentioned but looming background of present impurity, struggle, and death.

In the context of political terror the friendship between Potemkin and Zhirkova had certain Romantic connotations. In ways similar to German Romanticism, which cultivated friendship as a refuge from the egoism of the bourgeois world, these young Soviet citizens engaged in their mutual projections of virtue and purity in part to shield themselves from the polluting incursions of the political realm. However, Potemkin did not cultivate friendship as a polar opposite to the social sphere; on the contrary, he always insisted that personal feelings remain subordinate to his overriding commitment to build the new order.

zh: 一种象征性的生活

children: 在写给日尔科娃的一封信中，波特姆金提醒她：“你看，人生来不是只为了随便活完一生，而是为了通过他的存在让世界变得更美好。而这，离开了对完美的追求，对理想人格和理想社会的追求，是不可能实现的。”波特姆金试图将自己实现为他那个时代的模范人格，这符合利季娅·金兹堡的象征性行为概念。象征性行为发生在历史人格类型与特定个体之间的交汇点。一个人越是将普遍化的理想人格类型的特征融入自身，他的行为就越具有象征性。金兹堡补充道：“真实生活中的象征化在历史转折点上表现得最为明显，此时具有新行为准则的‘新人’诞生……那时，人们特别关注个体人格。在这样的时代，最具‘符号性’和表现力的人是那些个人特征最符合所涉历史模型的人。”金兹堡追溯了19世纪俄罗斯思想家生活中的象征性行为，包括亚历山大·赫尔岑和维萨里昂·别林斯基，他们是在德国唯心主义精神中成长起来的，但却对其政治保守主义感到失望，并摸索出一种新的“现实主义”伦理，它更强调自我与世界的批判性互动。同样，波特姆金也经历了一个转折点，苏联政权开始推行一种新的理想人格类型，而他正是力求体现这种模范新人。像他的浪漫主义前辈一样，他利用“文献虚构”的媒介，特别是私人信件和日记，以此理想人格来展现自己。这些信件的主要目的不是出版，而是阐明新人格类型。
在金兹堡讨论的俄罗斯浪漫主义者中，在体现一种新的、民主的人格类型方面最坚持不懈的是文学评论家别林斯基。将自己重塑为初露端倪的现实主义时代模范新人的强烈愿望，可能部分源于别林斯基试图超越他卑微的社会背景，这使他与他知识圈中其他贵族成员区分开来。在波特姆金的案例中，他卑微的社会背景似乎也与他重塑自我的强烈追求相关联。事实上，在他追求自我完善的过程中，波特姆金明确并反复引用别林斯基。

In one letter to Zhirkova, Potemkin reminded her: “You see, the human being is born not for just any purpose, merely to live out his lifespan, but so that he can make the world better by his presence in it. And this is impossible without striving toward perfection, toward an ideal personality and [an ideal] society.” Potemkin’s attempt to realize himself as a model personality of his time fits Lydia Ginzburg’s notion of symbolic behavior. Symbolic behavior occurs at the junction between a historical personality type and a given individual. The more an individual imbues himself with the features of the generalized ideal type of personality, the more symbolic his behavior becomes. Ginzburg adds: “Real-life symbolization is most clearly evident at historical turning points when ‘new men’ with new principles of behavior are born . . . when especially close attention is paid to individual personality. The most ‘semiotic’ and expressive people at such times are those whose individual features are best suited to the historical model in question.” Ginzburg traced symbolic behavior in the lives of nineteenth-century Russian thinkers, including Alexander Herzen and Vissarion Belinsky, who had grown up in the spirit of German idealism but were disappointed with its political conservatism and groped toward a new, “realist” ethics that put greater emphasis on a critical engagement of the self with the world. In similar fashion, Potemkin lived through a turning point when the Soviet regime began to deploy a new ideal type of personality, and it was this model new man that he sought to embody. Like his Romantic forebears he used the medium of “documentary fiction,” personal letters and the diary in particular, to represent himself in terms of this ideal personality. The chief purpose of the letters was not publication but the articulation of the new personality type.

Of the Russian Romantics discussed by Ginzburg, the most persistent in incarnating a new, democratic personality type was the literary critic Belinsky. The acute desire to remake himself into an exemplary new man of the dawning realist age may have stemmed in part from Belinsky’s attempt to transcend his modest social background, which separated him from the other, aristocratic members of his intellectual circle. In Potemkin’s case, too, his lowly social background seems correlated with the intensity of the quest to remake himself. And in fact in his quest for self-perfection Potemkin explicitly and repeatedly cited Belinsky.

与日尔科娃的通信充满了对别林斯基关于人格和个人自我实现的观点的引用，此外，作为他在乌拉尔矿业学院学习的一部分，波特姆金用摘录自他阅读别林斯基著作的内容填满了两本笔记本。作为一名革命民主主义者和人道主义者，以及社会主义现实主义美学的先驱，别林斯基在1930年代中期和后期的苏联文学和教育讨论中经常被引用，那个时期也见证了关于他的书籍出版量的激增。波特姆金曾参加文学社并遇到他梦想中的女孩的斯维尔德洛夫斯克图书馆以别林斯基的名字命名。在与日尔科娃的通信中，波特姆金提到了别林斯基关于“精神友谊”和“精神结合”的概念，将其视为自我实现的源泉和生命的本质。他曾写信给她：“只有当我致力于歌德、别林斯基和其他人时，我的灵魂才是鲜活和平静的。只有他们能让我的灵魂从日常利益的阴霾中升起，刷新对生活的感知，并照亮意识。我现在唯一的愿望就是投入你的怀抱，和你一起阅读别林斯基，和你一起思考和写作。”
波特姆金完全赞同别林斯基的真实生活理想，这种理想通过将主观自我提升到客观现实的层面来实现，体现在“社会”、“人类”和“历史法则”的普遍原则中。

The correspondence with Zhirkova abounds with references to Belinsky’s views on personality and personal fulfillment, and in addition, as part of his studies at the Ural Mining Institute, Potemkin filled two notebooks with excerpts from his readings of Belinsky. As a revolutionary democrat and humanist, and as a precursor of the socialist re-alist aesthetic, Belinsky was often cited in Soviet literary and pedagogical discussions of the mid- and late 1930s, a time that also witnessed a surge in the publication of books about him. The Sverdlovsk library in which Potemkin had attended the literary circle and met a girl of his dreams bore Belinsky’s name. In his correspondence with Zhirkova, Potemkin referred to Belinsky’s notion of “spiritual friendship” and “spiritual union” as the source of personal fulfillment and the essence of life. He once wrote to her: “My soul is alive and at peace only in those moments that I devote to Goethe, Belinsky, and others. Only they make my soul rise from the gloom of everyday interests, refresh the perception of life, and illuminate consciousness. My only wish now is to be in your embrace, read Belinsky with you, and think and write with you.”

Potemkin fully subscribed to Belinsky’s ideal of an authentic life to be reached through the elevation of the subjective self to the level of objective reality, embodied in the general principles of “society,” “humanity,” and the “laws of history.”

最重要的是，波特姆金以新人的姿态出现，并将这种姿态与一种道德承诺联系起来，呼应了别林斯基的情况。作为一名道德绝对主义者，别林斯基认为文学文本中阐述的道德思想只有在作者个人生活中完全践行时才有效。在他写给朋友的信中，别林斯基似乎故意展示他的道德人格，供自己和他人评判。波特姆金也同样谈到他渴望过一种具有历史范式意义的生活，鉴于这个计划所关涉的道德问题，他也感到有必要将其公开化。他曾在日记中写道，他希望“美丽地生活，让其他人可以从中学习”，并补充道：“我感觉我（总有一天）将站在社会法庭前，我的生活细节将被审查。我感觉自己正在接受审查。”

Most of all, the way Potemkin posed as a new man and connected this pose to a moral commitment echoed Belinsky’s case. A moral absolutist, Belinsky held that moral ideas expounded in a literary text were valid only if they were fully embraced by their author in his personal life. It seems that in letters to his friends Belinsky deliberately put his moral personality on display, open for himself and others to judge. Potemkin likewise talked about his desire to live a historically paradigmatic life, and given the moral stakes of this project, he also felt the imperative to make it publicly visible. He once noted in his diary that he wanted to “live life beautifully so that others could learn from it,” and added: “I feel that I will [one day] stand before the court of society, where the details of my life will be examined. I feel that I am under inspection.”

尽管波特姆金有意识地以别林斯基为榜样，别林斯基也将自己投射到波特姆金和年轻的苏联一代身上。1939年出版的一部关于别林斯基的专著以别林斯基的一段引言作为题词：“我们羡慕我们的子孙后代，他们注定会在1940年看到俄罗斯——屹立于文明世界之首，为科学和艺术提供法则，并接受所有开明人类的敬意。”因此，一场关于新人的对话将波特姆金和别林斯基跨越一个世纪的革命思想和实践联系起来，由于他们共同的历史意识，这场对话既可以顺着时间读，也可以逆着时间读。两者的立场唯一的不同在于，别林斯基认为自己只是新人的一个先行者。一百年后，恰好按别林斯基的时间表进行，波特姆金将自己描绘成一个活生生的新人，他已接近个人与社会之间的理想和谐。

While Potemkin consciously modeled himself on Belinsky, Belinsky also projected himself onto Potemkin and the young Soviet generation. A monograph on Belinsky published in 1939 featured as epigraph a quotation from Belinsky: “We envy our grandchildren and great grandchildren, who are fated to see Russia in 1940—standing at the head of the educated world, providing laws to science and art, and receiving tributes of respect from all enlightened humanity.” There was thus a dialogue on the new man connecting Potemkin and Belinsky across a century of revolutionary thought and practice, a dialogue that because of the historical consciousness they shared could be practiced in both chronological and reverse chronological order. The positions of the two differed only in that Belinsky perceived himself as a mere precursor of the new man. One hundred years later, and right on schedule according to Belinsky’s timeline, Potemkin portrayed himself as a living new man who had approximated the ideal harmony between the personal and the social.

在日记和与日尔科娃通信记录的时期之后，波特姆金仍然保持着对人格塑造的兴趣。1942年夏天，当他在高加索地区执行地质考察任务，大约在他兄弟弗拉基米尔（一名红军军官）在行动中失踪的同时，波特姆金写了一本名为《生活战略》的手册。这本小册子旨在为年轻的苏联男女提供关于“在社会主义时代，人格和生活应该是什么样子”的指导。那个时代是人类历史上第一次，整个社会都在“自觉和合乎规律的发展”道路上前进。这要求每个社会主义公民“参与解决你时代的社会问题”，并通过这样做提升自己，在思想和创造上达到时代的高度。在一个“血流成河”的战争时期，他的同辈人不断被杀害，波特姆金感到有必要将他那一代人在前十年获得的见解传给后代。

Potemkin retained his interest in personality formation beyond the period documented in the diary and the correspondence with Zhirkova. In the summer of 1942, while he was on a geological mission in the Caucasus and at about the time when his brother Vladimir, a Red Army officer, went missing in action, Potemkin wrote a manual entitled “Strategy of Life.” The booklet was to provide direction for young Soviet men and women on “what personality and life ought to be in the epoch of socialism.” That epoch was the first time in mankind’s history when a whole society proceeded on the path of “conscious and lawful development.” This demanded that each socialist citizen “become involved in solving the social problems of your time,” and in so doing rise  “ideologically and creatively to the heights of the epoch.” At a moment when “streams of human blood” were being shed in the war and ever more of his peers were being killed, Potemkin felt the need to pass on to future generations the insights his generation had gained in the previous decade.

这份文件清楚地表明，“新人”仍然是波特姆金理解自己和所处时代的核心。第一页刊登了普希金、别林斯基、海涅、高尔基、杰克·伦敦和尼古拉·奥斯特洛夫斯基等人的格言，颂扬一种富有表现力或英雄色彩的生活，并号召读者为实现他们的理想而奋斗。在开篇“社会主义革命提出了人格问题”之后，随后的部分列出了关于苏联新人特征的引文，大多附有出处（报纸或期刊——《真理报》、《共青团真理报》、《青年近卫军》，或苏联领导人——列宁、斯大林、日丹诺夫）。积极的性格特质，例如“坚定的马克思主义信念、钢铁般的意志力、内在的专注、果断、精确以及行动者伟大的朴实”，与过时的、资产阶级的性格特征并置：“过去的主观主义”、“庸俗主义”、“嫉妒”、“傲慢”、“阿谀奉承”、“颓废”、“痛苦”。这本小册子的其余部分列出了自我完善的推荐方法，包括掌握文化和科学、劳动合理化技术（包括计时和如何将工作与休息分开的建议）、意志训练、日常体操和身体自我控制。总而言之，波特姆金认为他的手册是为了建设共产主义社会和促进人类进步而进行有目的的思考和行动的号召，这些任务如此宏大，以至于“随心所欲”地生活是不可接受的。

The document makes it clear that the new man remained central to Potemkin’s understanding of himself and his time. The first pages featured aphorisms from, among others, Pushkin, Belinsky, Heine, Gorky, Jack London, and Nikolai Ostrovsky, extolling an expressive or heroic life and summoning readers to fight for the realization of their ideals. Following the opening remark, “The socialist revolution raised the question of personality,” a subsequent section listed quotations, mostly with references to a source (a newspaper or journal—Pravda, Komsomolskaya Pravda, Molodaya gvardia, or a Soviet leader—Lenin, Stalin, Zhdanov) on the features of the Soviet new man. Positive character traits, such as “an unwavering strength of Marxist convictions, iron willpower, inner concentration, decisiveness, precision, and great simplicity of people of action,” were juxtaposed to outdated, bourgeois personality features: “subjectivism of the past,” “philistinism,” “jealousy,” “arrogance,” “obsequiousness,” “decadence,” “suffering.” The remaining sections of the booklet listed recommended methods of self-perfection, including mastery of culture and science, techniques of labor rationalization (with suggestions on timekeeping and on how to divide work from rest), training of the will, daily gymnastics, and bodily self-control. All in all, Potemkin regarded his manual as a call for purposeful thought and behavior in the service of building a Communist society and advancing human progress, tasks of such magnitude that it was unacceptable to “live . . . ‘as you wish.’”

在这篇论述中，波特姆金将自己定义为尚未达到新人的理想：“我接受了高等教育，但我距离我所追求的目标仍然很远。愿未来的代表按照我梦想的方式生活。”他从历史角度解释了自己的不完美，称他所生活的时代仅仅是社会主义时代的黎明。早在20世纪30年代中期，他曾自信地宣称苏联的现在正在创造出像米洛的维纳斯一样美丽的人，但现在这一愿景获得了切实的未来主义意义。他现在指出，这个古典完美的时代“不远了；那时的人们将像米洛的维纳斯一样美好，而人际关系，用卡尔·马克思的话说，将像水晶一样清晰透明。”

尽管波特姆金的主观性是历史决定的，但他根据对自己个人发展的诊断重新评估了他对历史进程的看法。如果随着年龄的增长他没有变得越来越纯粹，这意味着历史并不像他之前认为的那样发展。他对自己不完美的新认识，形成于1942年，暗示着新人实际上尚未诞生。波特姆金的案例表明，新人的形象极难完全化身。作为一个理想，他似乎最明显地存在于人们努力接近他的过程中，但他无法被牢固而持久地占有。最终，共产主义主体性“正在进行中”的特点比对完美的追求更为重要，后者只会滋生忧郁和抑郁。

In this tract Potemkin defined himself as falling just short of the ideal of the new man: “I received a higher education, but I am still far from reaching that for which I strove. May the representative of the future live the way I dreamed of living.” He explained his imperfections historically, saying that the time he was living through was only the dawn of the socialist age. Back in the mid-1930s he had asserted with aplomb that the Soviet present was producing people as beautiful as the Venus de Milo, but now this vision acquired a tangible futurist sense. This time of classical perfection, he now noted, was “not far; a time when people will be as wonderful as Venus de Milo, and human relations, in the words of Karl Marx, will be clear and transparent, like rock crystal.”

While Potemkin’s subjectivity was historically determined, he re-evaluated his sense of the progression of history based on the diagnosis of his own personal development. If with increasing age he did not become steadily purer, this had to mean that history was not as developed as he had previously believed. His new sense of his imperfections, formulated in 1942, implied that the new man had in fact not yet been born. The figure of the new man, Potemkin’s case suggests, was extremely difficult to fully incarnate. As an ideal he seemed most palpably present as one struggled to approximate him, but he could not be firmly and durably appropriated. Ultimately, the work-in-progress character of Communist subjectivity was more important than the claim to perfection, which bred melancholia and depression.

波特姆金在斯大林时期的著作提供了对共产主义主体性的洞察——这一时期个人发展所期望和重视的特征，以及一个年轻的共产党员如何践行这些价值观并试图将其转化为传记内容。波特姆金从小就有写日记的习惯，但他抱怨日记的“主观主义”，它狭隘地关注他的内心世界，未能代表他所认同的“真实生活”，即劳动集体。他的自我评价在20世纪30年代中期发生了戏剧性的变化：当苏联政权宣布成功建立社会主义制度的基础并预示着“新”社会主义男女的出现时，他开始按照这个新理想来展现自己。他对自身形象的转变，得益于社会主义人格恢复了波特姆金认同为自己所有但之前曾被迫否认的特质，其中包括文化和敏感性，但他将这种转变解释为他自我的一种辩证发展。

Potemkin’s writings from the Stalin period provide insight into Communist subjectivity—the desired and valued characteristics of personal development during this period, and the way a young Communist engaged these values and sought to transform them into biographical substance. Keeping a diary from an early age, Potemkin complained about its “subjectivism,” its myopic focus on his inner world, and its failure to represent “real life,” which he identified with the laboring collective. His self-assessment changed dramatically in the mid-1930s: when the Soviet regime proclaimed its success in establishing the foundations of a socialist system and heralded the appearance of “new” socialist men and women, he began to present himself according to this new ideal. The shift in his picture of himself was facilitated by the fact that the socialist personality rehabilitated features, among them culture and sensitivity, that Potemkin recognized as his own but had previously felt compelled to disavow, but he explained the transition in terms of a dialectical progression of his self.

正如波特姆金反复强调的，对他而言，新人的本质不在于行为，也不在于外表或穿着，而在于他内在，在于他修养的灵魂。这一视角丰富了我们对第一代年轻苏联公民的理解，特别是那些被历史学家定义为追求外在文化和文明生活的“提拔分子”（vydvizhentsy）。在波特姆金的记述中，文化素养总是次于人格的培养，人格这一范畴涵盖了教育、道德追求、社会和政治活动以及审美表达。而“提拔分子”通常被描绘成机会主义者、新资产阶级，对苏联革命价值观漠不关心，波特姆金则始终以英雄和浪漫主义的笔触塑造自己。在努力改造和完善自己人格的过程中，他——部分自觉，部分不自觉地——将自己置于革命生命创造的谱系之中，这一谱系通过高尔基和尼采，追溯到19世纪30年代的俄国浪漫主义者，他们是首批探寻新人的人之一。

As Potemkin emphasized time and again, the essence of the new man for him lay not in behavior, nor in bodily appearance or dress, but within him, in his cultivated soul. This perspective enriches our understanding of the first generation of young Soviet citizens, notably the vydvizhentsy, whom historians have defined through their striving for outward culture and a civilized life. In Potemkin’s account culturedness always took second place to the cultivation of personality, a category that subsumed education, moral striving, social and political activism, and aesthetic expression. Whereas the vydvizhentsy are usually portrayed as careerist, neo-bourgeois, and aloof to Soviet revolutionary values, Potemkin consistently fashioned himself in heroic and Romantic terms. In striving to transform and perfect his personality, he in-scribed himself—in part consciously, in part unconsciously—in a genealogy of revolutionary life creation that reached back, via Gorky and Nietzsche, to Russian Romantics of the 1830s, who had been among the first to search for the new man.

波特姆金认为，理想情况下，共产党员应该通过持续不断的意识形态思考和行动，使自己永久置身于一个英雄的世界。他的自我实现理想——等同于他所说的“幸福”——是一种持久的超越状态，一种凌驾于日常生活的灰暗之上的更高现实。波特姆金在保持这种英雄模式方面比许多其他苏联日记作者更成功，但他未能避免失败和失误。他将这些失败解释为个人偏离了规定规范。他没有像一个完美的共产党员那样“以确定的平静燃烧”，拥有“持续灵感的平稳火焰”——这些都是完美共产党员的品质——而是不得不与他“热情、敏感的本性”抗争，这使他处于极度不稳定的情绪状态：“有时我被燃烧的狂喜点燃，我的心完全被情感点燃；另一些时候我被熄灭，仿佛我的心已经燃尽；我的能量消失了。”

Ideally, Potemkin believed, a Communist should make himself permanently at home in a heroic universe by means of uninterrupted, sustained ideological thinking and acting. His ideal of self-realization— tantamount to his notion of “happiness”—was a lasting state of transcendence, a higher reality towering over the grayness of daily life. Potemkin was more successful than many other Soviet diarists in in-habiting this heroic mode, but he was not spared failures and lapses. He interpreted these failings as personal deviations from a mandated norm. Instead of “burning with assured calm,” with the “smooth fire of constant inspiration,” attributes of the perfect Communist, he had to contend with his “passionate, sensitive nature” which subjected him to highly uneven emotional states: “At times I am set aflame by burning rapture, my heart completely blazing with emotion; at other times I am extinguished, as if my heart had burned out; my energy disappears.”

就像社会主义现实主义艺术一样，如果用模仿现有现实的标准来衡量，波特姆金的著作就无法被正确解读。社会主义现实主义力求捕捉一种不同的现实，即未来社会主义的完美现实，它在当下显现，更重要的是，是某个艺术家感受到它正在显现的。波特姆金首先试图表现的现实是其不断发展的革命意识及其对他的生活和环境的变革力量。对他而言，写作行为具有动员功能。他私密的著作既规定了完美人格的标准，也作为在自己的生活中实施这些标准的劝诫。他将这种干预性和变革性功能扩展到整个文学领域，包括小说和报纸报道：“不激发追求更美好、成为更好的人的文学，就不是文学。”

Like socialist realist art, Potemkin’s writings cannot be properly decoded if they are measured against a standard of mimetic representation of existing reality. Socialist realism strove to capture a different reality, that of future socialist perfection as it emerged in the present, and more important, as a given artist felt it to be emerging. The reality Potemkin sought to represent in the first place was that of his unfolding revolutionary consciousness and its transformative powers for his life and his environment. For him the act of writing performed a mobilizing function. His intimate writings both laid out standards of the perfect personality and served as exhortations to implement those standards in his own life. He extended this interventionist and transformative function to literature at large, including novels and newspaper accounts: “Literature that does not incite a striving toward the better, toward becoming a better person, is not literature.”
在他的自传体著作中，波特姆金以统一的方式描绘了他的一生，将他主观自我的成长嵌入十月革命和建设社会主义的故事中，并强调了主观和客观因素在他个人生活发展中的辩证互动。
苏联马克思主义神话的许多方面，对波特姆金的传记思想至关重要——一个关于贫穷、黑暗和受压迫的阶级获得解放并实现物质、智力和审美满足的神话——在他和他姐姐的生活中得到了经验性的证实。作为年轻、贫穷的村民，他们移居城市并获得了高等教育、政治意识和作为工程师的专业认可，他们是苏联梦想的活生生体现。波特姆金作为一名苏联公民所获得的生存满足感是不可否认的。

Throughout his autobiographical writings Potemkin portrayed his life in a uniform manner, embedding the growth of his subjective self in the story of the October Revolution and the building of socialism, and highlighting the dialectical interaction between subjective and objective factors in the development of his personal life.

Many aspects of the Soviet Marxist myth, so central to Potemkin’s biographical thinking—a myth of a poor, dark, and oppressed class that is liberated and gains material, intellectual, and aesthetic fulfillment—were empirically borne out in his and his sister’s lives. As young, poor villagers who migrated to the city and obtained higher education, political consciousness, and professional validation as engineers, they were living embodiments of the Soviet dream. The existential fulfillment Potemkin found as a Soviet citizen cannot be denied.

在他莫斯科公寓的一次会面中，波特姆金给我看了书柜里展示的另一块石头，就在花岗岩和大理石镇纸旁边。那是一块矿化海百合岩石，发现于乌拉尔山脉，表明数百万年前该地区曾被海洋覆盖。波特姆金评论说，和所有其他生物一样，人类死后也会矿化，而他们矿化的媒介就是他们的著作。这个引人注目的形象帮助我理解了波特姆金一生为何如此热情地写作，以及他为何如此精心保管他的个人档案。他生命的大部分时间都受到成为时代典范人物的道德使命的塑造，而写作是赋予这种典范人格以持久实质的方式。尽管他将自己的文本视为自我呈现的特权领域，但他同时也坚持其真实性、历史真实性和存在目的，从而反复跨越文本与经验生活之间的界限。
当我们结束最后一轮访谈时，列昂尼德·波特姆金声明我不能不带礼物就走。他递给我那块矿化海百合岩石，作为我们谈论他生活的纪念。

During one of our meetings in his Moscow apartment, Potemkin showed me another stone that was on display in his book cabinet, next to the granite and marble paperweight. It was a rock of mineralized sea lilies, discovered in the Urals and suggesting that millions of years ago the region had been covered by ocean. Potemkin remarked that, like all other living organisms, human beings became mineralized after their death, and the medium of their mineralization was their writings. This striking image helped me understand why Potemkin had written so fervently throughout his life and why he had invested so much care in preserving his personal archive. Much of his life was shaped by the moral mandate to become an exemplary personality of his time, and writing was a way to give enduring substance to this model personality. And while he viewed his texts as a privileged domain of self-representation, he also insisted on their reality, historical truth, and existential purpose, thereby repeatedly crossing the boundaries between text and experiential life.
As we finished our last round of interviews, Leonid Potemkin declared that I must not leave without a gift. He handed me the rock of mineralized lilies, in memory of our conversations about his life.

zh: 波特姆金日记，第5卷，第23背页（1935年2月4日后）。他经常在同一口气中使用“意义”和“美”这两个词，暗示共产主义的智慧力量与其美学吸引力是同义的。共产主义意识形态提供的全部意义等同于全部的美。
en:
Potemkin, diary, t. 5, l. 23ob (after 2/4/1935). He often used the terms
“meaning” and “beauty” in the same breath, implying that the intel-
lectual power of Communism was synonymous with its aesthetic
attraction. The total meaning afforded by Communist ideology
equaled total beauty.

zh: 同上，第10–10背页（1935年新年计划），15页（1935年1月23日），47页（1935年7月10日后），61、62页（1936年1月）；《书信》，第177–179页（给母亲的信，1936年11月22日）；《全联盟列宁主义共产主义青年团第十次代表大会速记报告》，第1册，第58–59页。
en:
Ibid., l. 10–10ob (New Year’s resolution, 1935), ll. 15 (1/23/1935), 47 (after
7/10/1935), 61, 62 (1/1936); correspondence, ll. 177–179 (letter to his
mother, 11/22/1936); Desiatyi s’’ezd, t. 1, 58–59.

zh: 波特姆金日记，第5卷，第47页（1935年7月10日后），55页（1935年9月28日后）。

在将自己塑造成“人类灵魂工程师”时，波特姆金似乎并没有考虑自己作为技术工程师的背景。虽然专业作家在斯大林社会作为人类灵魂工程师占据着特权角色，但技术工程师和建筑师创造了那个时代最令人难忘的美学丰碑：豪华的高层建筑、宏伟的人造水道（白海、莫斯科-伏尔加和费尔干纳运河）以及地下宫殿（莫斯科地铁）。正如一位参与费尔干纳运河建设的工程师所言：“雕塑家的喜悦是可以理解的，他将一块大理石变成了艺术品，几个世纪以来让观众充满喜悦。但一个将荒地变成繁花似锦的花园，将贫瘠地区变成幸福芬芳的绿洲的人，其喜悦要宏大得多”；见 N. 德米特里耶娃著，《美的审美范畴》，载《艺术》，1952年第1期，第78页。另见托马斯·拉胡森著，《生活如何写书：斯大林时代俄罗斯的现实社会主义与社会主义现实主义》（伊萨卡：康奈尔大学出版社，1997年）；沙滕贝格著，《斯大林的工程师》。
en:
In fashioning himself as an engineer of human souls Potemkin did
not seem to think about his background as a technical engineer.
While professional writers occupied a privileged role in Stalinist soci-
ety as engineers of human souls, technical engineers and architects
created the most memorable aesthetic monuments of the age, opu-
lent high-rises, grandiose artificial waterways (the Belomor, Moskva-
Volga, and Fergana canals), and subterranean palaces (the Moscow
metro). In the words of an engineer involved in the building of the
Fergana Canal: “The joy of the sculptor is understandable, who has
turned a block of marble into a work of art which for centuries fills
the viewer with joy. But how much more majestic is the joy of a man
who has turned dead land into flowering gardens, and destitute
regions into happy, fragrant oases”; N. Dmitrieva, “Esteticheskaia
kategoriia prekrasnogo,” Iskusstvo 1952, no. 1, 78. See also Thomas
Lahusen, How Life Writes the Book: Real Socialism and Socialist Realism in
Stalin’s Russia (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 1997); Schattenberg,
Stalins Ingenieure.

zh: 波特姆金日记，第5卷，第1页（1934年10月1日）。
同上，第4卷，第25背页（1933年1月11日）。
列昂尼德·波特姆金著，《辩证唯物主义与历史唯物主义（RGI三年级学生，L. 波特姆金）》，未注明日期的手稿（笔记本上的印章显示其生产于1935年）。
en:
Leonid
Potemkin,
“Dialekticheskii
i
istoricheskii
materializm
(st[udent] III kursa RGI, L. Potemkin),” undated manuscript (the
notebook bears a stamp showing that it was produced in 1935).

zh: 波特姆金日记，第5卷，第52、57–58背页（1935年9月28日后）。
同上，第98页。
与伊拉·日尔科娃的通信持续了三十多年；波特姆金访谈录，2002年4月20日。
en:
The correspondence with Ira Zhirkova went on for more than thirty
years; interview with Potemkin, 4/20/2002.

zh: 波特姆金著，《书信》，第76页（来自日尔科娃的信，1938年1月14日），第23页（致日尔科娃的信，1937年11月11日后），第62页（来自日尔科娃的信，1937年11月21日）。
en:
Potemkin, correspondence, l. 76 (letter from Zhirkova, 1/14/1938), ll. 23
(to Zhirkova, after 11/11/1937), 62 (from Zhirkova, 11/21/1937).

zh: 同上，第15、134页（致日尔科娃的信，1937年11月和1938年3月27日）。波特姆金提到的社会主义文化温室并不完全是隐喻性的。斯大林时代的文化以温暖和繁茂来表现自己，以强调其生命力抱负。在20世纪30年代，莫斯科到处都是出售冷饮和冰淇淋的小亭子，意在让冬天的城市看起来像避暑胜地。本着同样的精神，许多政府办公室都装饰着盆栽棕榈树。见弗拉基米尔·帕佩尔内著，《斯大林时代的建筑：文化二》（剑桥：剑桥大学出版社，2002年），第132–134页。
en:
Ibid., ll. 15, 134 (to Zhirkova, 11/1937 and 3/27/1938). Potemkin’s refer-
ence to the greenhouses of socialist culture was not entirely meta-
phorical. The culture of the Stalin era represented itself in terms of
warmth and lushness, to underscore its vitalist aspirations. In the
1930s Moscow was dotted with kiosks selling cold drinks and ice
cream, which were intended to make the wintry city resemble a sum-
mer resort. In the same spirit many government offices were deco-
rated with potted palm trees. See Vladimir Papernyi, Architecture in the
Age of Stalin: Culture Two (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press,
2002), 132–134.

zh: 波特姆金著，《书信》，第61页（致日尔科娃的信，1937年11月24日后）。
同上，第18页（来自日尔科娃的信，1937年11月11日），第22–27页（致日尔科娃的信，1937年11月）。
同上，第85、112–113页（来自日尔科娃的信，1938年2月2日，3月2日）。我感谢简·普兰珀建议使用“乌托邦式忧郁”一词。
en:
Ibid., ll. 85, 112–113 (from Zhirkova, 2/2/1938, 3/2/1938). I thank Jan
Plamper for suggesting the term “utopian melancholia.”

zh: 同上，第139页（致日尔科娃的信，1938年4月13日），第128页（致日尔科娃的信，1938年3月9日）；波特姆金著，《生活策略》，第8页。
en:
Ibid., l. 139 (to Zhirkova, 4/13/1938), l. 128 (to Zhirkova, 3/9/1938);
Potemkin, “Strategiia zhizni,” l. 8.

zh: 波特姆金著，《书信》，扉页。
同上，第100–101页（致日尔科娃的信，1938年3月20日）。
波特姆金日记，第5卷，第11页（1935年1月）；《书信》，第52页（来自日尔科娃的信，1937年11月24日）。
en:
Potemkin, diary, t. 5, l. 11 (1/1935); correspondence, l. 52 (from Zhir-
kova, 11/24/1937).

zh: 波特姆金著，《书信》，第123页（致日尔科娃的信，1938年2月23日）。利季娅·金兹堡（Lydia Ginzburg）著，《论心理散文》（普林斯顿：普林斯顿大学出版社，1991年），第16、60页。
en:
Potemkin, correspondence, l. 123 (to Zhirkova, 2/23/1938). Lydia Ginz-
burg, On Psychological Prose (Princeton: Princeton University Press,
1991), 16, 60.

zh: 波特姆金著，《书信》，第8、73–74、130页（致日尔科娃的信，1937年11月，1938年1月，3月9日）。关于别林斯基，见例如：A. 马林金著，《狂热的维萨里翁》，载《青年近卫军》，1936年第6期；G. 布罗夫曼著，《论别林斯基与普希金》， 同上；A. 布勃诺夫著，《论 V. G. 别林斯基》，载《小火炬》第16期（1936年6月30日）；A. 拉夫雷茨基著，《别林斯基的现实主义》，载《十月》，1936年第6期；G. 布罗夫曼著，《伟大的批评家》，载《新世界》，1938年第6期；I. G. 阿夫图霍夫著，《V. G. 别林斯基的教育观点》，载《苏联教育学》，1938年第6期。这些出版物中没有一篇，也没有任何在共青团第十次代表大会上引用别林斯基的发言者，直接将他作为苏联人格形成的理想。这是波特姆金自己的贡献。
en:
Potemkin, correspondence, ll. 8, 73–74, 130 (to Zhirkova, 11/1937, 1/
1938, 3/9/1938). On Belinskii see, e.g., A. Malinkin, “Neistovyi Vis-
sarion,” Molodaia gvardiia, 1936, no. 6; G. Brovman, “O Belinskom i
Pushkine,” ibid.; A. Bubnov, “O V. G. Belinskom,” Ogonek, 16 (6/30/
1936); A. Lavretskii, “Realizm Belinskogo,” Oktiabr’, 1936, no. 6; G.
Brovman, “Velikii kritik,” Novyi mir, 1938, no. 6; I. G. Avtukhov, “Peda-
gogicheskie vzgliady V. G. Belinskogo,” Sovetskaia pedagogika, 1938, no.
6. None of these publications, and none of the speakers who cited
Belinskii at the Tenth Komsomol congress, invoked him directly as
an ideal for Soviet personality formation. This was Potemkin’s own
contribution.

zh: 波特姆金大量的别林斯基摘录包含在两个笔记本中：“V. G. 别林斯基”和“V. G. 别林斯基。第2卷（1840–1842）”。
en:
Potemkin’s copious excerpts from Belinskii are contained in two
notebooks: “V. G. Belinskii,” and “V. G. Belinskii. Tom 2 (1840–1842).”

zh: 在这一条目中，波特姆金倾诉了他对自己不爱的女人的身体欲望。他很庆幸自己没有与她发生关系，保持了“精神上的纯洁”，并补充道：“也许她将不得不向人们（社会）讲述我的事。”见波特姆金日记，第5卷，第84背页–85页（1936年夏或秋）。这是一个有力的迹象，表明监控结构——被谴责为不道德从而也被视为政治上不可靠的危险——如何融入了他过一种道德生活的渴望。
en:
In this entry Potemkin confided his physical desire for a woman he
did not love. He was relieved that he had not become involved with
her and had preserved his “spiritual purity,” and he added: “Perhaps
she will have to tell the people (obshchestvu) about me.” Potemkin, di-
ary, t. 5, ll. 84ob–85 (summer or fall 1936). This is a telling indication
of the way surveillance structures—the danger of being denounced as
immoral, and hence also as politically unreliable—fed into his desire
to live a moral existence.

zh: M. 约夫丘克（M. Iovchuk）著，《别林斯基：其哲学与社会政治观点》（莫斯科：社会经济出版社，1939年），第3页。别林斯基称自己是“被时代诅咒压垮的倒霉一代，邪恶的时代！……新一代令我高兴：它充满活力，没有反省的腐朽习惯。”见金兹堡著，《论心理散文》，第79–81页。
en:
M. Iovchuk, Belinskii: ego filosofskie i sotsial’no-politicheskie vzgliady (Mos-
cow: Sotsekgiz, 1939), 3. Belinskii referred to himself as a member of
“an unlucky generation weighed down by the curse of its time, an evil
time! . . . The new generation gladdens me: it is full of life and devoid
of the rotten habit of introspection.” Ginzburg, On Psychological Prose,
79–81.

zh: 波特姆金著，《生活策略》，第6–6背页、3页。夹在小册子里的零散笔记表明，波特姆金想利用这些文本和他与日尔科娃的信件进行更大规模的出版，形式可以是通信集，或者是关于当前个人生活理想和人类新形式的讨论。同上，第2背页。
en:
Potemkin, “Strategiia zhizni,” ll. 6–6ob, 3. Scattered notes stuck in-
side the booklet indicate that Potemkin wanted to use the text and
his correspondence with Zhirkova for a larger publication in the form
of a correspondence or a discussion on current ideals of personal life
and the new forms of humanity. Ibid., l. 2ob.

zh: 同上，第4、10–11背页、3、5背页、6背页。波特姆金引用了据推测其自练指令所借鉴的书籍：门德尔松著，《意志的培养》；内恰耶夫著，《意志力及其培养》[原文如此]；安德烈耶夫著，《自我控制日记》。见同上，第27背页、31背页、39页。
en:
Ibid., ll. 4, 10–11ob, 3, 5ob, 6ob. Potemkin cited books from which his
self-training instructions were presumably borrowed: Mendel’son,
Vospitanie voli; Nechaev, Sila voli i sr. ee vosp-ia [sic]; Andreev, Dnevnik
samokontrolia. Ibid., ll. 27ob, 31ob, 39.

zh: 同上，第3背页、7背页。
同上，第6背页；波特姆金日记，第5卷，第76–76背页（1936年8月）。
en: Ibid., l. 6ob; Potemkin, diary, t. 5, ll. 76–76ob (8/1936).

zh: 格罗伊斯著，《斯大林主义的总体艺术》，第55–56页。波特姆金访谈录，2004年4月11日。
en: Grois, Total Art of Stalinism, 55–56. Interview with Potemkin, 4/11/2004.

zh: 他以几乎相同的方式描绘了他家人的传记；见波特姆金著，《亲缘之源》，第129、141、155页。
en:
He cast the biographies of his family members in much the same
light; Potemkin, “Rodnye istoki,” 129, 141, 155.
